relationships.subject: Pm1a
relationships.evidence_quote: Application of Pm1a (10 nM) or Pm2a (10 nM) to mouse DRG cells caused an immediate and sustained increase in fluorescence indicative of increased intracellular Ca2+ concentration

relationships.subject: Pm1a
relationships.evidence_quote: Consistent with the results of our calcium imaging experiments using mouse DRGs, both Pm1a and Pm2a are potent modulators of mNaV1.7.

relationships.subject: Pm2a
relationships.evidence_quote: By contrast, Pm2a caused a large sustained current (at 1 μM: 1.00 ± 0.14 of peak; p = 0.0002, paired t test), with an EC50 of 2.6 ± 0.7 μM

relationships.subject: TTX
relationships.evidence_quote: Pm1a- and Pm2a-induced spontaneous nocifensive behaviors in mice were completely (Pm1a; p < 0.0001, unpaired t test) and partially (Pm2a; p = 0.0005, unpaired t test) ameliorated by injection of 2 μM TTX

key_findings: Harvester ant venom peptides Pm1a and Pm2a cause long-lasting nocifensive behavior in mice by activating TTX-sensitive Nav channels, shifting Nav1.7 activation to hyperpolarized potentials.
Pm2a additionally modulates TTX-resistant Nav1.8 and Nav1.9, whereas Pm1a is selective for TTX-sensitive subtypes.
